item.title: ‘TRUE CLUB’: Pinner cycling club spins back into action for new term
item.description: Pedals at the ready, Field End Flyers Community Cycle Club will be back from its winter break on Saturday, February 28, and is welcoming new young riders to join the fun. item.title: ‘WE APOLOGISE’: Northwood gym vow to take ‘member privacy seriously’ following concerns
item.description: A Northwood gym has apologised for its failings after a female gym goer felt her privacy was invaded in the changing rooms. The gym member, who wishes to remain anonymous, left the David Lloyd Northwood branch on Saturday, January 31. She says her privacy was invaded by people taking photos and videos. item.title: ‘REAL DIFFERENCE’: Garston families invited to join groundbreaking baby DNA study
item.description: A few drops of blood taken moments after birth could change the course of a child’s life – and families in Garston now have the chance to be a part of that breakthrough. West Hertfordshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust announced on Tuesday, January 20, that it joined the world-leading Generation Study, led by Genomics England […]Read More →

item.title: ‘SUPREME ENERGY’: Iconic Ovaltine calendar shortlisted for Object of the Year
item.description: Some things are simply timeless, and a remarkable 1967 Ovaltine calendar proves it is always a good date to celebrate a great design. Produced at the iconic Kings Langley factory, the calendar has been shortlisted for Hertfordshire Museums Object of the Year. item.description: Confusion has arisen among some residents after an alleged brochure stated that a second Aldi would open last summer at the former Iceland and Laser Planet units in the town centre, but this has yet to happen. item.title: ‘WELL ATTENDED’: Residents enjoy film at French inspired event in Chorleywood
item.description: Residents enjoyed a special screening of the film The Marching Band earlier this month, as part of a joint event run by Chorleywood Film Club and Chorleywood French Twinning Association. item.description: Families you may be born into or choose, and others – like the NHS – never let you go. item.description: Charlotte Bankes, from Hemel Hempstead, and Huw Nightingale claimed Team GB’s second gold medal today (Sunday, February 15) in the Olympic Winter Games Milano 2026.
